title: Burp Business Logic — WSTG-BUSL: Race Conditions, Workflow Abuse, Mass Assignment
body: WSTG-BUSL has 9 tests and is the hardest to automate. No scanner can find business logic flaws — every request is valid HTTP, only the sequence, quantity, or context makes it abuse. Race conditions (Turbo Intruder single-packet attack), workflow bypass, mass assignment, negative values, upload abuse, and price manipulation are the eight patterns. The Boolean box confirmed:false mass assignment is a BUSL finding at its core: a business control (account activation) bypassed by exploiting the framework's attribute-setting behaviour.
cmd:
# ══ ⭐ BUSINESS LOGIC — manual reasoning, scanner-blind ══════════════
# WSTG-BUSL (9 tests). No scanner can find these — every request is valid.
# Only the sequence, quantity, or context makes it abuse.
# The single most underrated OSCP web category.

# 1) MASS ASSIGNMENT — the Boolean box technique (BUSL / IDNT overlap)
# The recognition chain (both pieces from Burp):
#   REQUEST has user[email]=x  ->  model name (user) + syntax (user[field])
#   RESPONSE has "confirmed":false  ->  field exists, controls business logic
#   EXPLOIT: add user[confirmed]=true to the request body
# Why it works: framework sets any attribute you pass (user[field]=value)
# unless the developer explicitly whitelists allowed fields.
# If "confirmed" isn't in Rails' permit() or Laravel's $fillable, you own it.
# Every JSON response field is a candidate. All of them.
user[confirmed]=true    user[admin]=true      user[role]=admin
user[verified]=true     user[is_admin]=1      user[email_verified]=true
user[approved]=true     user[balance]=1000    user[plan]=premium

# 2) RACE CONDITIONS (WSTG-BUSL-09) — Turbo Intruder
# Win a race: two simultaneous requests processed as if both are the first
# Target: any "one-time use" action: discount/coupon code, gift card, free trial,
#         transfer/withdrawal, vote, referral bonus, limited-stock purchase
# Detection: manually trigger the action twice in rapid succession -> does it work twice?
# Exploitation with Turbo Intruder (built-in single-packet attack):
#   HTTP History -> right-click the request -> Extensions -> Send to Turbo Intruder
#   Select template: examples/race-single-packet-attack.py
#   Set concurrency (200 simultaneous requests)
#   Run -> observe: if the action succeeds more than once, race condition confirmed
# Classic exploit: discount code (10% off)
#   Send 50 simultaneous APPLY_COUPON requests -> coupon applied 50 times
#   Balance goes negative or order total drops to 0
# Withdrawal race:
#   Account has $100. Send 20 simultaneous withdraw $100 requests.
#   If no atomic lock -> $100 withdrawn 20 times -> negative balance

# 3) WORKFLOW BYPASS — skip steps in a multi-step process (WSTG-BUSL-03/04)
# Map the intended flow by browsing it once legitimately:
#   /cart -> /checkout -> /payment -> /payment/confirm -> /order/complete
# Then test direct access to later steps WITHOUT completing earlier ones:
#   Browse to /payment/confirm directly after /cart -> no payment taken?
#   Browse to /order/complete -> order placed for free?
# Registration bypass (the Boolean box chain without mass assignment):
#   /register -> /verify-email -> /dashboard
#   Try: GET /dashboard directly after POST /register -> skips verification
#   Try: POST /register with is_admin=true in the body
# In Burp: record the full flow in HTTP History -> identify the final confirmation
#          request -> send it to Repeater -> remove intermediate steps -> replay

# 4) NEGATIVE VALUES / BOUNDARY TESTING (WSTG-BUSL-05/06)
# Any numeric input (quantity, price, transfer amount, item count):
quantity=-1       # negative quantity -> reverse the transaction?
quantity=0        # zero -> free item?
quantity=99999    # overflow -> integer wrap or performance impact?
price=0           # if price is a client-submitted field -> order for free
price=-1          # negative price -> store credit?
# In Repeater: modify the numeric field -> observe the response and any downstream effects
# Also test strings where numbers expected: quantity=abc, quantity=null, quantity=[]

# 5) UPLOAD ABUSE (WSTG-BUSL-08/09)
# Beyond extension bypass (see file_upload node):
#   IDOR + upload: can you upload a file INTO another user's directory?
#     /api/upload?user_id=2 -> change to user_id=1 -> overwrite victim's file
#   Double upload: same filename uploaded twice -> does it overwrite? race condition?
#   Path traversal in filename: ../../uploads/shell.php -> server stores it at shell.php
#   Zip slip: craft a .zip containing a file with path traversal name:
#     ../../../etc/cron.d/evil -> extracted to /etc/cron.d/evil
#   Content-type mismatch: upload .php but claim Content-Type: image/jpeg
#     -> some servers trust the MIME type, not the extension

# 6) FORCED BROWSING / FUNCTION-LEVEL AUTHZ (WSTG-ATHZ-02 overlap)
# Admin/internal functions discovered in JS or ferox -> test while low-priv:
/api/admin/users          -> GET all users (mass disclosure)
/api/admin/export         -> download database export
/api/internal/config      -> application configuration
/api/users/{id}/promote   -> promote user to admin role
# Test each: logged in as regular user -> does the server check the role?
# Also test without any session (unauthenticated):
curl -s http://$ip/api/admin/users    # no cookies at all

# 7) BURP MACROS — automate multi-step flows ════════════════════════════
# When Intruder/Scanner needs CSRF tokens refreshed between requests:
# Project options -> Sessions -> Macros -> Add
# Record: the sequence of requests that fetches a fresh CSRF token
# Session Handling Rule: "Run a macro" -> select your macro -> "Update only these params"
#   -> enter the CSRF token parameter name
# Now Scanner/Intruder automatically refreshes the token before each request
# Essential for: authenticated scanning, brute force behind CSRF protection

# 8) PRICE MANIPULATION (WSTG-BUSL-06)
# Any e-commerce or checkout flow: is the price validated server-side?
# Add item to cart -> intercept the checkout POST in Burp -> look for price field
# If price=99.99 is in the body -> change to price=0.01 -> does order go through?
# Also try modifying the item ID to a cheaper item while keeping the product name
warn: WSTG-BUSL is where the most interesting OSCP web vulns hide and where most testers stop looking. Race conditions on one-time-use actions (coupons, transfers, votes) are reliably exploitable with Turbo Intruder's single-packet attack — 200 simultaneous requests reveal the flaw instantly. Workflow bypass requires understanding the intended flow first (browse it once), then testing each step independently. Mass assignment needs both the request syntax AND the response fields — getting only one half means you miss the exploit.
